question: Is the Aurzen TravelPlay a good back seat screen for a Tesla Model Y? Where can I buy one?
query: Aurzen TravelPlay review Tesla Model Y compatibility where to buy

replays.text:
**It could be a good fit if you want a portable movie screen for parked-car use—but it isn’t a standalone rear-seat display.** TravelPlay is a foldable, clip-in projector screen and sunshade. It offers rear-seat, tailgate, and panoramic-roof setups, with roughly 47- and 50-inch panels, and comes with a carry bag. You’ll need a **separate compatible projector**; it’s not for watching while the car is moving. [Aurzen’s product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y)

**Check your Model Y’s year before buying:** Aurzen says it’s designed for the **2025–2026 Model Y Refresh** and warns fit may vary on earlier versions. The product page lists it at **$119.99** and says it’s available in the U.S. only. [Buy it from Aurzen](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y)

It folds up and installs with clips. You’ll need a separate compatible projector, and projection is for use **only while parked**. So I’d consider it for a refreshed Model Y and occasional parked movie nights—not as a driving-time entertainment screen or a simple plug-in display.
